full_judgment:
Ahmed Sohel J : On an application of the petitioner under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 497 days, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the delay of 497 days in filing the Appeal against the judgment and decree dated 21-1-2007 (decree signed on 28-1-2007) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 292 of 1997 dismissing the suit, should not be condoned. 

 6. In support of his submission he cited a case of Anu Bala vs Upazila Nirbahi Officer Perojpur, reported in 43 DLR 611, wherein it has been held that ‘Condonation of delay in a case filed by the Government and the State need to go by the limitation applicable to all, but if the case by the Government is delayed, some consideration need be allowed considering the fact that even in the case of filing appeals, the Government remains a slow moving juristic person.’ 

 8. We have gone through the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act filed by the petitioner and given our profound attention to the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate of the petitioner, Government of Bangladesh. 

 9. Now for the better understanding of section 5 of the Limitation Act, the said section is quoted below:— 

 ‘Any appeal or application for a revision or a review of judgment or for leave to appeal or any other application to which this may be made applicable by or under any enactment for the time being in force, may be admitted after the period of limitation prescribed thereof, when the appellant or applicant satisfies the Court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within such period.' 

 "In dealing with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, in the case of the Government, public interest has to be duly considered and various authorities, formalities and complications are involved and, as such, Government require a longer time in making the decision and acting on it. If, on behalf of the Government, a reasonable explanation of delay is given, there is no reason why it should not be accepted."
